subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures preserve the asynchronous accepted `sessions_spawn` contract with typed/logged terminal failure state, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight Docker startup enough to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: That choice affects the public spawn contract, registry/session state, gateway waits, and the overlapping lifecycle PR, so automation should not pick the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add typed logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagent list, and agent wait paths.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough Docker startup validation before acceptance to reject immediately, accepting extra latency and compatibility implications.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open as the sandbox-specific repro while resolving the broader startup lifecycle direction in the related open lifecycle issue and PR.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add typed logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagent list, and agent wait paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans subagent API behavior, session lifecycle, and compatibility, and Peter has the clearest feature-history signal for those seams.
